items.summary_ko: vault-java-driver는 세 가지 경우에 TLS 인증서와 호스트명 검증을 조용히 끈다. 그 경우 모든 인증서를 신뢰하는 SSLContext가 설치되며, 네트워크 경로상의 공격자는 전송 중인 Vault 토큰과 시크릿을 읽고 응답을 위조할 수 있다. 영향 버전은 5.2.0~6.2.3이며 7.0.0에서 수정되었다(CVSS 7.4, HIGH).
items.content_ko: vault-java-driver는 HashiCorp Vault용 Java 클라이언트로, 검증을 요청했는데도 TLS 인증서와 호스트명 검증을 조용히 끄는 세 가지 경우가 있다. 첫째는 build()를 호출하지 않고 VaultConfig에 전달한 SslConfig이고, 둘째는 Java 역직렬화로 복원한 SslConfig이며, 셋째는 VAULT_SSL_VERIFY를 1, yes, on처럼 “true”가 아닌 참값으로 설정한 경우다. 세 경우 모두 SslConfig.isVerify()가 false를 반환하고 드라이버는 모든 인증서를 신뢰하는 SSLContext를 설치한다. 이때 네트워크 경로상의 공격자는 Vault 토큰과 시크릿을 전송 중에 읽고 응답을 위조할 수 있다. 영향 버전은 5.2.0~6.2.3이며 7.0.0에서 수정되었다. CVSS 7.4(HIGH)로 표기되어 있고, 공개일은 2026-11-05다.

items.title: Guerrilla bike lanes: San Francisco makes illicit infrastructure permanent (2016)
items.content:
When two cyclists were tragically  killed in hit-and-run collisions this past summer, a group of anonymous urban activists known as the San Francisco Transformation Agency erected a set of protected bike lanes using traffic cones. Usually such  guerrilla interventions are temporary. They raise awareness but ultimately get taken down by municipal authorities. But when the same group recently (and illegally) installed a set of soft-hit posts alongside Golden Gate Park, the city reacted by  making the change official .

The SFMTrA , a play on the city’s Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA), “is a collective organization of men and women committed to making streets safer for cyclists and pedestrians, and doing it quickly.” According to the organization, their members use tactical urbanism to accomplish a range of objectives, including:

Provide a real safety increase for cyclists and pedestrians.

Draw attention to areas of the city that are unsafe for vulnerable pedestrians and cyclists.

Put pressure on the SFMTA and public officials to make proactive, rapid and substantive improvements in street safety.

Many of their interventions involve orange traffic cones , which do grab visual attention but are also impermanent and easily damaged. Adding more robust traffic delineators (also known as soft or safe hit posts) may have helped persuade the city to retain this particular recent installation along John F. Kennedy Drive.

“Generally, we have no choice but to remove cones and posts that do not go through an official process,” wrote the city agency in a statement , “because it’s a code violation to place objects in the roadway, and they could create conflicts for various types of traffic.” But in this case, they plan to install official safe hit posts and leave the temporary ones in place until their review process is complete.

Image via the Reasonably Polite Seattleites

Guerrilla activists in other cities have tried similar things with mixed results. When the group  Reasonably Polite Seattleites installed a similar set of delineators along a stretch of road in Seattle, the city initially took them down. Subsequently, though, officials wrote the activists an exceedingly nice response and eventually agreed to reinstall the posts.

Image via the Reasonably Polite Seattleites

City traffic engineer Dongho Chang of the Seattle Department of Transportation explained that a combination of issues (including the height of the posts and state control of the street) forced the removal at first. At the same time, he acknowledged the “time, money and risk” invested by the group and even offered to give the posts back. He later followed up with a letter indicating the city and Washington State Department of Transportation  would put the delineators back in place.

In New York City, a perhaps less-polite group has been known to take things even further by building out entire bike lanes from scratch. After a local community board rejected plans to extend an extant lane, Right of Way took to the streets at night to paint their own. As a catalyst, the group cited an accident that took place after a taxi driver struck a pedestrian (after reportedly arguing with a cyclist sharing the lane).

Guerrilla interventions like these can provoke a variety of responses from critics and cities alike. In some cases, tactical urbanists are celebrated by communities but also  jailed or fined  by officials for their actions. In other instances, though, such installations can give a city an opportunity to publicly support a direction of change. In San Francisco, which has already built out 27 miles of protected bike lanes over recent years, the city seems to be signalling it is open to progress .
items.title_ko: 샌프란시스코, 불법 자전거 도로를 영구 시설로 전환 (2016)
items.summary_ko: 2016년 기사다. 자전거 이용자 두 명이 뺑소니 사고로 숨진 뒤 익명의 도시 활동가 단체 SFMTrA가 교통 콘으로 보호형 자전거 도로를 설치했다. 이후 이 단체가 골든게이트 공원 옆에 불법으로 설치한 유연한 기둥을 시가 공식 시설로 바꿨다.
items.content_ko: SFMTrA는 샌프란시스코 교통국(SFMTA)을 비튼 이름으로, 자전거 이용자와 보행자를 위해 거리를 더 안전하게 만드는 데 헌신하며 이를 빠르게 해내는 남녀의 집단 조직이라고 스스로를 소개한다. 이 단체는 전술적 도시주의(tactical urbanism)를 활용해 자전거 이용자와 보행자의 실질적인 안전 향상, 위험한 구역에 대한 관심 환기, SFMTA와 공무원에 대한 신속하고 실질적인 개선 압박을 목표로 한다고 밝혔다. 주황색 교통 콘은 눈에 잘 띄어 이런 개입에 자주 쓰인다. 게릴라식 자전거 도로는 대개 임시 조치로 끝나고 시 당국이 철거하지만, 이번에는 불법으로 설치된 기둥을 시가 정식 시설로 인정했다는 내용이다. 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist
items.content:
North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist

'It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident,' exchange says

FBI pins $6.3B Binance crypto heist on North Korean hackers

Google says Asian advertisers spending less due to Europe's customs changes

In the year AI re-wrote the infosec rulebook, it’s comforting to know crypto exchanges still have bad security

Attackers turn GitHub issues into supply chain campaign against 61 public repos in less than an hour

China's spaceplane bears striking resemblance to America's X-37B

North Korean cryptocurrency thieves tricked a Binance software engineer into downloading malware onto their work-issued computer during a fake job interview process before last week's record-breaking $6.3 billion heist .

In an incident report published on Tuesday, the cryptocurrency exchange said several techniques - including social engineering via fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method” - led to the October 29 security breach.

“Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” the incident report said. “It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident.”

Over the weekend, the FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation linked to Lazarus Group , known for combining espionage with massive cryptocurrency heists . The Pyongyang-backed crew is also highly adept at job market scams - both posing as IT workers , who are then hired by Western companies , and as potential employers to lure software engineers into downloading malware and infecting corporate devices .

With the recent Binance attack, the Norks used the latter.

The attack prep began back in June with a supply chain attack when one of its engineers downloaded a malicious Homebrew installation . While the malware was detected by the security team, the device was replaced, and all affected credentials rotated, “Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker,” the report says.

Three months later, the social engineering part of the attack happened.

In September, another software engineer was contacted via a “legitimate job-hunting platform” by someone purporting to be a project director who arranged a series of job interviews for the Binance engineer with the fake company. During the first round - a live video interview with the engineer and a fake HR rep - the interviewer “shared a social media account with him, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in order to build trust,” according to the report. “This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches.”

The second interview with someone purporting to be the CEO of the phony company was conducted on a “popular social chat app,” and toward the end, the CEO instructed the engineer to download an “assignment” containing a malware-laced code repository. The code executed on his work computer during the setup process, which kicked off a series of unauthorized activities.

According to Binance, the malware replaced a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version, which executed commands and established communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The attackers also took steps to hide the malicious script and evade detection, and it worked. Binance’s endpoint security tools did not immediately detect the malware.

CREATE  /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv_

DELETE  .../libexec/pyenv  (3,344 B)      ← remove the valid pyenv

RENAME  pyenv_ → pyenv  (3,414 B)  ← replace it with a malicious version

DELETE  /opt/homebrew/bin/pyenv  (3,414 B)

ln  (create a new symlink)  +  spawn zsh

Then, on October 20, the miscreants used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to the computers of wallet DevOps engineer A…

items.title: Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links
items.content:
Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links

Content shared with anyone who has the URL will be scanned for 'harmful content,' though the iMaker hasn't defined that term

Hey, Siri: Plug into my app like you said you'd do way back in 2024

Apple's Mac business is booming, but the memory market has other plans

Darkbloom, which allowed Mac users to rent out their GPUs for AI inference, warns of low payouts

GM cracks the petty cash box for multistate driver tracking settlement

Apple takes powerful M6 chip to the MacBook Pro, iMac

If you share content using public iCloud links, Apple could soon be looking over your shoulder and checking for "harmful content." The iBiz announced plans to moderate publicly accessible iCloud share links in version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS on a support page published on Tuesday. To clarify, this applies only to iCloud content shared via links created to be accessible to anyone, as opposed to content shared directly with other people.

“Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content,” Apple explained on the new help page without bothering to define what harmful content means. Based on the wording, it appears those checks will apply to all iCloud items shared using "Anyone with the Link," which Apple says it can also access. The company hasn't explained how the checks will work.

The share-with-anyone option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, Apple said, even if Advanced Data Protection , Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled for the account.

“If you try to upload harmful content, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete the content at any time,” the help page continues, adding that the iMaker may also block or disable accounts associated with harmful content.

The company also said it reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary, suggesting that its undefined "harmful content" category could include child sexual abuse material (CSAM), malware, and other potentially unlawful content.

Without a proper definition of what it defines as harmful, however, iCloud users are essentially left at Apple’s mercy: If it chooses to continue to bend the knee to the Trump administration, for example, content deemed objectionable by the standards of political figures could end up wiped out.

Apple also hasn't explained whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will be responsible for identifying and removing so-called harmful content, or whether any decisions will be left to AI, which can easily be fooled into making a bad moderation call.

The scanning of such content, as mentioned above, begins with version 27.3 of Apple’s various OSes, which were released to developers in beta on Tuesday, with a general release expected in December.

Apple didn’t respond to questions for this story. ®
items.title_ko: Apple, 공개 링크로 공유된 iCloud 콘텐츠에 ‘유해 콘텐츠’ 검사 도입 계획
items.summary_ko: Apple은 iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS 27.3부터 ‘링크가 있는 모든 사용자’와 공유된 iCloud 항목을 ‘유해 콘텐츠’ 여부로 검사한다고 지원 문서에서 밝혔다. 이 검사는 특정인과 직접 공유한 콘텐츠가 아니라 공개 링크로 공유한 콘텐츠에만 적용된다. 다만 Apple은 ‘유해 콘텐츠’의 정의를 밝히지 않았다.
items.content_ko: Apple은 화요일 게시한 지원 문서에서 iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS 27.3 버전부터 공개 iCloud 공유 링크를 검사하겠다고 밝혔다. 문서에 따르면 ‘Anyone with the Link’ 방식으로 공유된 항목은 Apple이 ‘유해 콘텐츠’가 있는지 확인한다. 이 적용 대상은 링크를 누구나 열 수 있도록 만든 콘텐츠에 한정되며, 특정인과 직접 공유한 콘텐츠는 포함되지 않는다. Apple은 지원 문서에서 ‘유해 콘텐츠’가 무엇인지 정의하지 않았다. 기사는 이 조치가 사용자 공개 공유 콘텐츠에 대한 감시 우려로 이어질 수 있다는 점을 짚었다. 본문 일부에는 다른 Apple 관련 기사 제목들이 함께 실려 있어 이 기사의 핵심과는 구분해서 봐야 한다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: How to speed up the Rust compiler in November 2026
items.summary: compilers, rust
items.content:
My first month working on Rust compiler performance for

Hexcat is over and it’s time to see some of what’s

Spans are a critical data structure in the Rust compiler. Every AST, HIR, and

MIR node carries a span. Each span has four fields recording the following.

A source location ( lo and hi ). A crate’s source files are concatenated

into a single buffer, and these are indices into that buffer.

Possibly some hygiene and provenance data ( context ), relevant for macros

Possibly an extra relative position ( parent ) that is used to minimize the

compile time impact of small changes to source locations, such as those

caused by inserting a single line at the start of a file.

Each of the four fields is 32 bits, resulting in 16 bytes of data. But most of

the time these 16 bytes can be compressed into one of three 8-byte inline

formats, and the remaining cases are interned into a global table. This works

by taking advantage of patterns in the data: many source locations have a small

length (i.e. a small difference between lo and hi ); many spans have a zero

context and/or parent, and the non-zero contexts and parents are typically

small integers; parents are only used in incremental builds.

the old compression scheme with one that is simpler and more efficient. For

incremental builds we now typically intern around 1% of spans compared to

20-40% with the old scheme. (In non-incremental builds we typically intern

fewer than 0.1%.) Also, we can always store the context field inline even in

the interned case, which is useful because we often read the context by itself.

This change reduced instruction counts across many benchmarks, in the best

cases by more than 3%, and the cycle count improvements were even higher.

Incremental builds saw the largest improvements due to less interning.

instruction counts across many benchmarks, in the best case by more than 2%.

using a pattern type to give Span a niche so that Option<Span> would be the

same size as Span . It worked but didn’t help performance because we don’t use

Option<Span> much, and it made the code more complicated. So I abandoned it.

encoding/decoding and stable hashing we typically need to get information

about the same parent span from a hash table over and over. In this PR I put a

single-entry cache in front of that hash table, which avoids the hash table

lookup in most cases. This reduced instruction counts on many benchmarks, in

the best case by more than 4%, mostly benefiting incremental compilation.

In these three PRs I focused on the compilation time of

in-development new trait solver is slower than the old trait solver. I did

a dozen or so micro-optimizations across the three PRs, such as early returns

on hot paths, avoiding allocations, avoiding some recomputations, and

optimizing some special cases. These reduced the instruction count overhead of

the new solver on a Check Full build from 1.49x to 1.16x, and other new

solver benchmarks like typenum and nalgebra also saw improvements. There is

still more work to be done but this is good progress.

case, reducing instruction counts for many benchmarks, in the best case by over

the AttrTokenStream and AttrTokenTree types. These mirrored the

widely-used TokenStream and TokenTree types but were only used for cfg

processing. This change was mostly about making the code simpler, but it also

avoided some token stream conversions, reducing instruction counts on a range

of benchmarks: by 4% on the deep-vector stress test, and by less than 1% on

the creation of one type variable per element in literals requiring type

inference like vec![1, 2, 3, 4] . This was a huge win (8-12% cycle count

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Ripple-65B Preview: U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding
items.content:
Achieving U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding

Achieving U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding

Ricursive Intelligence is a full-stack artificial intelligence lab building self-improving systems by co-optimizing hardware, software, and model.

To power our chip design platform, we trained a language model from scratch that sets a new U.S. open-weight SOTA on agentic coding. We optimized the model architecture for our training and serving platforms, driving substantial efficiency gains.

Today, we release Ripple-65B Preview , a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers our AI chip design platform. The model is pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with support for up to 1M context length. Ripple-65B Preview delivers strong results on agentic coding, achieving U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art (80.52) on TerminalBench 2.1 and surpassing significantly larger US open-weight models such as Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4), Thinking Machines Inkling 975B (63.8), and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (56.4).

Ripple’s dense model architecture provides strong reasoning performance with low-latency token generation. The model’s small parameter envelope also enables it to run efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark, which feature high compute FLOPs with low memory bandwidth relative to datacenter accelerators.

Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face , Together AI , GMI Cloud , and OpenRouter . Fireworks goes live later today.

LLM pretraining is legendarily expensive. In 2023, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said that GPT-4 training costs exceeded $100 million . In the following year, Dario Amodei said that frontier AI models can cost up to $1 billion to train, projecting that costs would rise to $10-100B by 2026 to 2027 for pretraining alone.

In contrast, we developed and trained Ripple-65B Preview for only $32M, which is one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding , as estimated to the best of our knowledge. ¹ Note that $32M is our full R&D cost starting from scratch, including pretraining ladder development, data mixing, evals, debugging, synthetic data generation, posttraining recipe development, and the final hero pretraining and posttraining run.

Rather than investing in a brute-force RL climb, we carefully iterated on our SFT and RL recipes with a focus on compute efficiency. We opted not to buy any posttraining data, instead devising our own synthetic data pipelines, quality filtering, and coverage metrics.

Our mixed RL recipe uses truncated importance sampling , score centering , and linear length penalty with high-quality long-horizon synthetic environments. The RL tasks are tuned for our model capabilities, and we continuously added harder tasks as the model improved. The end result was a steep RL climb from a strong initial SFT checkpoint. We reached a TerminalBench 2.1 score of 80.5 with only 1.4M rollouts, roughly 70x fewer rollouts than Reflection Beam, the prior SOTA.

Ripple-65B Preview’s architecture was designed to be trained and served efficiently on NVIDIA hardware. A key objective was to make design decisions which reduce pretraining and posttraining infrastructure complexity while still enabling strong reasoning and agentic performance. Therefore, we chose to train a modernized dense Transformer model rather than use Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) like other labs. This decision quickly paid off, and we were able to train a strong model from scratch while maintaining a solid MFU (40%) throughout pretraining and posttraining, even with simple sharding, no custom kernels, and no quantization.

Ripple-65B Preview uses a thin-and-deep model aspect ratio, with a narrow d_model (5120) and 80 total layers. To improve reasoning performance, we overprovision the number of attention heads while increasing the SWA-to-global layer ratio and reducing SWA window size to compensate for the increased cost. items.title: C++26 Disapproved
items.content:
On October 23, 2026, the unthinkable happened. It was supposed to be a mere formality: C++26 was up for a vote by the ISO National Bodies (NBs). The options are always approval, rejection, or abstention. Comments are also allowed. Since 1998, this process had run quietly and smoothly. Not so on October 23, 2026. After a twelve-week voting period, the result is in: Disapproved !

I would like to mention here that I am a member of the C++ Standardization Committee and, together with my colleagues, represent Germany’s vote. ISO rules also stipulate that certain votes are internal to ISO, and the results—or the breakdown of the results—may not be published. This article contains my own personal views.

As far as I know, this is the first time in the history of C++ that DIS ballot failed. When I searched the ISO system, I could only find one other DIS that was not approved: ISO/IEC DIS 26926 C++/CLI Language Specification dated August 11, 2006. It’s possible that my search privileges aren’t sufficient to view everything, but all ISO programming languages should be visible to me. The sad end of ISO/IEC DIS 26926: the project was halted. I mention this upfront to clarify the significance of this vote.

In the following, I will use various terms from everyday ISO terminology. At https://isocpp.org/std/iso-iec-jtc1-procedures , there is an overview of the various stages of an ISO standard. DIS is the penultimate stage. As the overview also shows, a two-thirds majority is required. This majority was not achieved.

The reason for the rejection is quite clear from the comments submitted by the National Bodies (NBs): contracts. Put simply, a number of NBs believe that this feature is not yet ready for release.

Now it gets complicated. The C++ Standardization Committee, also known as WG21, follows ISO rules but also has some additional rules. One of these is (or was) that opinions are always heard whenever new information becomes available. If an opinion was heard and a feature was nevertheless not changed as desired, the person respects the outcome and accepts that many others disagree.

However, the voting body at the NB level may also consist of other individuals, or the NBs are, of course, free to vote differently.

The previous practice was that NBs would only vote against a standard if new information became available or if errors in the process or similar issues were identified. This changed on October 23, 2026.

It’s difficult to judge in this complex situation; the NBs who want C++26 without Contracts argue that there is new information. I myself find it hard to share this view. A new paper with old arguments is not new information to me.

The feature has been on the wish list for a long time. I was already in the room in Cologne back in 2019, at the time for C++20, when Contracts, in a different form back then, were being included in the standard. I was also in the room when the feature was removed from C++20 again during the same meeting. As a result, a study group was formed to address the topic of Contracts and its various aspects from 2020 to approximately 2024. Afterward, the study group submitted its work and proposals to the Evolution Working Group (EWG), the central body for language extensions. There, the topic was discussed further over several meetings before being included in C++26 by a majority vote.

In the next step, WG21 voted on the C++26 draft in March 2026, which included Contracts. Here, too, a large majority was achieved, though not without dissenting votes.

And that brings us to the next phase: DIS. At this stage, there were enough “no” votes that a two-thirds majority was not reached.

items.content_ko: 본문에 따르면 C++26 투표는 원래 형식적인 절차로 여겨졌으나, 12주간의 투표 끝에 2026년 10월 23일 부결되었습니다. 투표 옵션은 승인, 반대, 기권이며 의견 제출도 가능합니다. 1998년 이후 이 절차는 조용하고 순조롭게 진행되어 왔다고 합니다. ISO 규정상 일부 투표는 내부 용도로만 쓰여 결과나 세부 내역이 공개되지 않을 수 있습니다. 필자는 검색 권한이 충분하지 않아 일부를 못 봤을 수 있다고 덧붙이며, ISO 시스템에서 찾을 수 있는 승인되지 않은 DIS는 2006년 8월 11일자 ISO/IEC DIS 26926 C++/CLI 언어 명세뿐이었고 그 프로젝트는 중단되었다고 전합니다. 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있습니다.

Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 1: A new exploit, which is even worse than this one is currently doing rounds on telegram. Details unknown at this time. Unpatched at the time of writing.

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

A logical flaw in Meta’s AI-powered Instagram account recovery assistant let attackers bypass two-factor authentication entirely not by cracking a code or intercepting an SMS, but by talking the chatbot into doing the work for them. High-value “OG” Instagram handles worth hundreds of thousands of dollars were stolen and resold on Telegram within minutes of each compromise. The dormant Obama White House account got hijacked. Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

items.title: Insects don't swarm at LED lights
items.content:
Insects swarm at gas station light, July 2006 , (photo by cgpgrey , CC BY 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons)

Remember when you used to encounter swarms of insects around outdoor electric lights? Their well known attraction to outdoor lights is used by entomologists and moth lovers to conduct insect surveys. All you need is a light and a white sheet to see who’s flying at night.

Light trapping for insects at Maui (photo by Forest & Kim Starr , CC BY 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons)

Nowadays, if you want to attract insects, you have to be picky about the light you use. As everyone changes over to LED lights, we see the color difference but we can’t see the crucial difference in insect attraction between incandescent and LED.

Odd one out, LED streetlight by John Goldsmith , CC BY-SA 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

Our guide Roland Rumm on the WINGS Veracruz trip explained what happens with insects in the switch to LED lights. His family has an outdoor dining space that is well lit with artificial light. As a child he loved to watch the geckos climb to the lights and eat the insects. (This gecko can change to a bland gray color when he needs to.)

Bay Island least gecko looking colorful (photo by Laura Gaudette , CC BY 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons)

In recent years the family changed over to LED lights and the geckos disappeared. Were the geckos gone? No. But far fewer insects were attracted to the LED lights so the geckos had no reason to show up.

In 2024 the BBC wrote about Why insects are drawn to artificial light at night :

Flying insects use moonlight to navigate. Since the moon is always above them, they orient themselves so that the light shines on their backs. That’s how they stay upright in flight.

Moonlight contains ultraviolet (UV) and infrared wavelengths because it is merely reflected sunlight. Insects cue on UV, believing it to be the moon. When artificial lights transmit UV they look like moonlight so insects orient their backs to it. Consequently they circle the light and even flip upside down when the artificial light is pointing up to the sky!

Incandescent lights transmit UV but LEDs do not. Insects are far less attracted to LED.

In 2016 scientists at the University of Bristol, UK ran experiments to compare insect attraction to four types of light : Incandescent (tungsten filament), Compact fluorescent, “Cool-white” LED and “Warm-white” LED.

We conducted field experiments to compare the relative attractiveness of four commercially available “domestic” lights, one traditional (tungsten filament incandescent) and three modern (compact fluorescent, “cool white” LED and “warm white” LED), to aerial insects, particularly Diptera. We found that LEDs attracted significantly fewer insects than other light sources, but found no significant difference in attraction between the “cool” and “warm white” LEDs. Fewer flies were attracted to LEDs than alternate light sources, including fewer Culicoides midges (Diptera: Ceratopogonidae). Use of LEDs has the potential to mitigate disturbances to wildlife and occurrences of insect?borne diseases relative to competing lighting technologies.

— Experimentally comparing the attractiveness of domestic lights to insects: Do LEDs attract fewer insects than conventional light types?

Here’s what they found. NOTES: CFL = Compact fluorescent, FIL = incandescent (the old lightbulb), LEDC = LED cool white, LEDW = LED warm white light.

Average insect trap catch in the “evening” sampling periods commencing at sunset (17 sites). Lights were compact fluorescent (CFL), tungsten filament (FIL), light?emitting diode “cool?white” (LEDC), and light?emitting diode “warm?white” (LEDW). Error bars indicate SE. From: Experimentally comparing the attractiveness of domestic lights to insects: Do LEDs attract fewer insects than conventional light types?

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: France plans internet tax of 5.5 cents per gigabyte
items.content:
Internet content providers would have to pay a fee based on the amount of data they deliver over the internet to end users in France. A proposal submitted by the French Socialist Party (Parti socialiste, PS) in France’s National Assembly is currently sparking debate.

The idea behind the planned new tax is that companies that host content on their servers for users to access over the French web would have to pay the tax. The rate would be 5.5 cents per gigabyte delivered to end users in France. Large tech companies would pay most of the tax, as the PS says they account for a substantial share of internet traffic in France. The French Socialists cite data from French telecom regulator ARCEP in their proposal , according to which Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix and cloud provider Akamai account for half of France’s internet traffic. ARCEP estimates that 200 billion gigabytes of data travel each year over the infrastructure of French internet providers. The new tax would be capped at 2% of a content provider’s total revenue, or 15% of its revenue generated in France. It is worth noting that the proposal explicitly refers to revenue, not profit. The Socialists argue that such a tax could bring about €10 billion into France’s treasury.

Internet providers would help collect the tax

Internet providers would play a central role under the plan. They would have to collect anonymized data on internet traffic so each affected company could be taxed correctly. The proposal’s sponsors see no data privacy concerns. They say the content of the data would never be examined, nor would any personal information, such as data about subscribers to content services. Only the amount of data would be recorded. Still, some users may object to their connection data potentially ending up in logs for the French tax authorities. The proposal’s sponsors do not explain exactly what the stored data would look like.

If a company uses a content delivery network (CDN) to cache content close to end users — for example, a streaming provider seeking to give customers the best possible connection — the amount of data delivered by the CDN would be treated as the amount of taxable data.

The proposal does not distinguish between companies based on size, even though such a distinction is explicitly made, for example, in the EU-wide “Digital Services Act” (DSA). Under the law, a “very large online platform” (VLOP) is one used by an average of 45 million EU residents per month. That amounts to 10% of the people in the European Union. However, the VLOP designation applies only to EU regulation, not regulation by individual member states.

The goal of the new tax is to make global players in the digital economy pay more. The proposal’s sponsors argue that the current tax system gives these companies substantial advantages over other sectors of the economy. However, the proposal does not specify which companies would be subject to the new fee. Although it refers to global digital companies and major players such as Meta and Amazon, it does not identify the business models it is targeting. In theory, any company with one or more IP addresses that offers content for users to access online could be affected.

Some companies already see themselves as affected by the possible new tax and are pushing back. VideoLAN has already issued scathing criticism of the French Socialists’ proposal. The nonprofit organization is behind the well-known free VLC media player, the widely used x264 video codec, and various other video codecs and software libraries. VideoLAN says the new tax would cost it more than €1 million a year. The company does not explain how it arrived at that figure. It would mean, however, that VideoLAN would have to pay tax on around 18 million gigabytes of French internet traffic. In addition to VLC client downloads, this could include data associated with VideoLAN’s video codecs and software libraries.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-123025 📢 Source: mitre 💣 CVSS Score: 9.4 (CRITICAL) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True An OS Command Injection vulnerability was discovered in the Google Cloud DNS validation module of the OPNsense os-acme-client plugin through 4.17. The DnsGcloud::prepare() method decodes the dns_gcloud_key model field and directly interpolates the string fields gcloud_account and gcloud_project into a shell command passed to proc_open() via LeUtils::run_shell_command() without any validation or escaping. A remote authenticated user with privileges to issue or renew certificates through the WebGUI/API can achieve arbitrary code execution as root. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-05T06:29:05.916Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123025
items.title_ko: OPNsense os-acme-client 플러그인 Google Cloud DNS 모듈 OS 명령 주입 취약점 (CVE-2026-123025, CVSS 9.4)
items.summary_ko: OPNsense os-acme-client 플러그인(4.17 이하)의 Google Cloud DNS 검증 모듈에서 OS 명령 주입 취약점이 발견되었다. 원격의 인증된 사용자가 WebGUI나 API를 통해 인증서를 발급하거나 갱신할 권한을 가지고 있다면 root 권한으로 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있다. CVSS 점수는 9.4(CRITICAL)이며 원격 공격이 가능하다고 명시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: OPNsense os-acme-client 플러그인 4.17 이하 버전의 Google Cloud DNS 검증 모듈에서 OS 명령 주입 취약점(CVE-2026-123025)이 발견되었다. DnsGcloud::prepare() 메서드가 dns_gcloud_key 모델 필드를 디코딩한 뒤, gcloud_account와 gcloud_project 문자열 필드를 검증이나 이스케이프 없이 LeUtils::run_shell_command()를 거쳐 proc_open()에 전달되는 셸 명령에 직접 삽입한다. 공격자는 WebGUI나 API를 통해 인증서를 발급하거나 갱신할 권한이 있는 원격의 인증된 사용자이기만 하면 root 권한으로 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있다. CVSS 점수는 9.4(CRITICAL)이며, 원격 공격 가능 여부는 True로 표시되어 있다. 출처는 MITRE이며 게시일은 2026-11-05다.
